items.title: Euro FX futures hold near 1.1650 as CVOL ticks higher.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures traded near unchanged on Thursday, hovering around the 1.1650 level after drifting lower from last week's highs above 1.17. The market continues to take its cues from U.S. Dollar strength, even as expectations remain for a 25 bps rate hike from the European Central Bank next month. Volatility steadily edged higher throughout the week, reflected in the CVOL index, as traders position themselves for the Jackson Hole economic symposium. Friday's session will bring additional data points, including the Chicago Purchasing Managers index and University of Michigan sentiment, though market attention remains squarely on the scheduled 9:00 a.m. address from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

In the energy sector, WTI crude oil extends a technical bounce amid geopolitical tensions that are impacting Russian supply. Looking ahead, the market anticipates Friday's pivotal Jackson Hole address from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh for clues on monetary policy, while also digesting a $44 billion Treasury auction, ongoing corporate earnings and key economic data including Tokyo CPI and U.S. consumer sentiment.

items.title: Euro FX futures slide as inflation data supports dollar.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures experience a near-term pullback following their late August cycle high, navigating a mix of U.S. inflation figures and supportive European economic data. Core PCE in the U.S. held firm at 3.3% year-over-year, keeping higher-for-longer interest rate debates active and providing underlying support for the dollar. Conversely, the euro finds some domestic strength as August PMI figures reflect improving manufacturing conditions, led by Germany. Additionally, German second-quarter GDP saw an upward revision to 0.3%, potentially easing recessionary fears and providing the European Central Bank with flexibility to maintain restrictive policy.

items.title: Crude breaks $80 as Iran exports plunge.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down the latest market moves, noting U.S. equities opening lower with Nasdaq futures leading the decline. Economic data comes in mixed as core durable goods miss forecasts while headline numbers surprise to the upside. PCE inflation and second-quarter GDP both match expectations, keeping the Federal Reserve's rate path in focus ahead of key Jackson Hole speeches. In energy, crude oil breaks below $80 as U.S. sanctions and a blockade drive a sharp drop in Iranian exports, despite ongoing diplomatic mediation. Plus, a look ahead at upcoming Treasury auctions, key tech earnings and jobless claims data.

items.title: From escalation to exit ramp: why oil's war premium is unwinding again
items.excerpt: Key Points: Crude prices have fallen sharply as Iran-Oman talks, Pakistani mediation and other signals raise hopes that Washington and Tehran are searching for a way to de-escalate. The price move is running well ahead of the physical recovery, with Hormuz vessel traffic still severely depressed and Gulf energy infrastructure remaining disrupted. Diesel and gasoil cracks have fallen from extreme peaks but remain exceptionally elevated as Gulf refinery outages and Russian export restrictions continue to constrain supply. The biggest downside risk is a meaningful reopening of Hormuz, while the upside risk is that markets have priced a diplomatic breakthrough that proves much harder to deliver. items.title: Euro futures held near 1.1675 ahead of key economic data.
items.excerpt: Todd Colvin analyzes the recent price action in Euro futures, which rallied to close near 1.1675, a level they have hovered around since last Wednesday. He discusses how the dollar's recent weakness propelled the euro to two-month highs, although prices have now steadied. Colvin also highlights the CVOL index, noting that volatility remains unchanged as the market anticipates tomorrow's PCE index and the upcoming Jackson Hole Economic Symposium. Finally, he breaks down the latest positioning data, pointing out that speculators are maintaining their net short positions in anticipation of a potentially firmer dollar following this week's key macroeconomic announcements.

items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the morning's market action, highlighting a slight bounce in U.S. equities led by Nasdaq futures. Crude oil falls to an eight-session low, breaking below $82 per barrel as traders price out geopolitical risk from recent U.S. sanctions on Iran and weigh softer Chinese demand. Looking ahead, focus shifts to the upcoming July PCE inflation data, where the market will look for any signs of reaccelerating inflation that might influence expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike. The market also prepares for a slate of corporate earnings alongside crucial economic reports, including durable goods orders and the latest Q2 GDP estimate.

items.title: The many rewards of investing responsibly
items.excerpt: At its core, responsible investing is an investment approach that incorporates additional information about environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks and opportunities alongside traditional financial analysis. While it has come under pressure lately, the core idea remains compelling and the case for aligning investment decisions with long-term ESG outcomes remains relevant. Responsible investing has faced increasing criticism in recent years. Some sustainable funds have lagged broader market indices, concerns about greenwashing have shaken investor confidence, and political opposition, particularly in parts of the United States, has slowed progress on ESG regulation globally and made it harder for some investors to pursue responsible investing strategies. items.title: British Pound futures reach 6.5-month highs on weaker dollar.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners analyzes the currency markets, noting that British Pound futures rallied for a third consecutive session to reach six-and-a-half-month highs. Despite mixed U.K. economic data showing a 0.5% drop in July retail sales alongside a rising composite PMI, the pound continues to find support. Iaccino highlights that the bigger driver for the currency is coming from the U.S. side, where softer economic data and Treasury buyback plans are easing Fed expectations and putting pressure on the dollar.
